Decision: leave WriteChapters sequential, don't implement parallel. Measured on a real smoke test (9 chapters, karpathy/micrograd, direct Anthropic API bypassing caveman-proxy): sequential 562.3s vs parallel 521.0s, a ~7% wall-clock gain. Far short of the review's anticipated N-x speedup -- Anthropic's own per-account rate limits partially serialize concurrent calls, and wall-clock is bounded by the single slowest chapter. 7% doesn't justify the real costs: lost narrative continuity (chapters can no longer literally continue prior prose), max_workers=total needing a cap for larger repos, and retry semantics degrading from 'redo one chapter' to 'redo the whole fan-out'. Message Batches API also considered and ruled out separately -- it trades latency for cost (up to 1hr, max 24hr turnaround), wrong tradeoff for a single interactive tour generation. Working prototype (uncommitted, branch prototype/parallel-writechapters in agent worktree) available if repo size/chapter count grows enough to revisit.

Fixed in PR #105, merged as 5fe9d71. ResponseTruncated derives from SystemExit, so it leaves the retry loop everywhere at once. Tour keeps its handler for the chapter context but no longer converts.

Three things came out of implementing it that the bead did not anticipate:

1. Bypassing the retry loop bypasses exec_fallback, and OverviewNode depends on that hook for its documented optional-overview promise (coderay-q2r.13). coderay-cvi had already broken that for PromptTooLarge -- a live defect on main, proven by test_overview_stays_non_fatal_when_the_prompt_is_too_large failing before the fix. OverviewNode.exec now catches DETERMINISTIC_FAILURES and delegates to its own exec_fallback.

2. The Gemini branch reported every non-STOP finish reason as a truncation. Verified against the SDKs types.py that only MAX_TOKENS is the output cap; SAFETY, RECITATION, LANGUAGE, OTHER, BLOCKLIST, PROHIBITED_CONTENT, SPII and MALFORMED_FUNCTION_CALL are content and function-call blocks, several sampling-dependent. Once a truncation left the retry loop, one content block would end a Gemini run on the first attempt advising a knob that cannot fix it. Split so only MAX_TOKENS raises ResponseTruncated.

3. ProfileEras, Graveyard and TableDeepDive accumulated batch results locally and persisted only in post, so a mid-batch failure left nothing in run_state.json. Not a regression (identical before and after, and the disk cache means a re-run pays only for the call that failed) but a real gap, so all three now grow the list in shared as results arrive, like WriteChapters.
